A gap listed here has been looked at on a map, traced back to what the
steward wrote at each end, and agreed. It is put into the graph before
the closing step runs, so a later repair elsewhere in the survey cannot
A pinned gap is still a gap. Nobody walked it, it is not boundary, it is
counted as gap in every figure and drawn as a gap on every map. Pinning
settles where it runs, not what it is.

note: The Savahun boundary with Anaje clan, 953 m, between two points Max
Mamo named himself. North: the hook where the Karira boundary ends and
he wrote 'Sawahun broudre with anaje clan'. East: the Guaipnun
waterfall, where three recordings stop and he wrote 'Savahun big drain
so hard to continue over', 'Guaipnun hard to cross over.' and 'guapnun
waterfall'. He could not get across.
Tested against the terrain model for a river route and there is none:
the two ends are in different catchments whose flow paths first meet
4.4 km downstream. No modelled channel comes within 600 m of the line.
This stretch needs walking. It is not to be closed by drawing.
203 m between two named places, with nothing walked between them.
South: 'Butam do' (Unido Ose), which Prut Buitari writes 'But am doa'.
North: 'Muamara' (Unido Ose). Both notes sit 1-2 m from the chord's
Both stewards walked this boundary together — their lines run on top of
each other everywhere else — and both stopped at Butam do and both
resumed at Muamara. The middle of the gap is 85 m from any walked line.
Two stewards stopping at the same place is worth asking the clan about.
